tasks.short: Change funeral services around community needs and viable delivery

steps.what: Review service uptake, prices, costs and recorded requests for funeral service changes
inputs: actual service bookings and requests recorded by arrangers
finance-maintained service costs and prices
outputs: checked service demand and cost comparison

steps.what: Discuss unmet community needs and practical service delivery with community contacts and staff
inputs: checked service demand and cost comparison
actual community contacts and service staff

steps.what: Choose changes to service offerings, prices and implementation timing using the actual needs and capacity
inputs: heard needs and delivery constraints
checked service demand and cost comparison
outputs: manager-written service choices, prices, resource requirements and effective dates

steps.what: Prepare the complete revised service catalogue entries from the manager's explicit choices
inputs: manager-written service choices, prices, resource requirements and effective dates
existing service catalogue structure
outputs: complete draft catalogue revision with prices and effective dates

steps.what: Check delivery readiness and approve the exact final service catalogue revision
inputs: complete draft catalogue revision with prices and effective dates
manager-written service choices, prices, resource requirements and effective dates

steps.what: Save the approved revised service offerings in the same operational catalogue
inputs: approved catalogue revision v1

steps.what: Brief staff on implementing the changed services and resolve delivery questions
inputs: effective service catalogue revision
actual staff delivery questions
outputs: staff understanding of changed service delivery

tasks.design: Configure service and cost views in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, then populate catalogue fields from the manager's explicit choices. The manager tests community fit and delivery readiness before approving and saving a final revision, then briefs staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful demand, cost and service descriptions can sit in separate views; this is not evidence of manual rekeying at any particular home.
tasks.enabler_now: Native filtered reports and catalogue templates can reuse existing fields without interpreting bereaved families' needs.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding which services are respectful, affordable and deliverable needs local judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Listening to community preferences and refusing commercially attractive but unsuitable offers.

ambition.what: Review whether a specific underused service meets a documented community need each quarter.

reach.task: Assess the contribution of a proposed service
reach.learn: Interpret fully allocated costs and capacity constraints.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for service and finance access; consult staff if recording practices change

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: service catalogues can hold versioned descriptions, prices and effective dates, while native reports filter existing transactions.

assumptions: Boundary is manager planning and implementing catalogue changes, including staff explanation; actual individual funeral delivery is separate. Overlap with pricing and staff-policy tasks must be resolved in roll-up.

Arrangers already produce dated booking rows with service code and request category; finance produces costs with period and basis. Missing or unstructured needs are gathered in s2 and captured in s3, not inferred by a free extraction step.

Test native reports and catalogue templates first. s4 only assembles explicit chosen fields; it never invents an offering or price. If fields are absent, manual entry stays within s3/s4 and savings fall.
All shares and retained percentages are provisional design scenarios, not measured baselines. The same-system save takes approximately no time; its required one-point share stays fully retained.
Catalogue publication to an external website is not assumed; any later external publication needs its own final-version gate.
unknowns: Existing catalogue versioning and quality of service coding
research_questions: Can existing views reproduce one checked service comparison without new data capture?
Which catalogue entries require free drafting rather than field assembly?

already_counted.description: Check assembled catalogue fields and effective dates

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue field mappings and report filters

approvals.approved_version: approved catalogue revision v1; any edit requires renewed s5 approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 17.2 minus 1 upkeep gives 16.2. High allows 3.2 additional hours for catalogue exceptions; low applies when native views and templates already remove this effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Negotiate and issue prearranged funeral contracts

steps.what: Retrieve the current prearranged funeral service terms, price options and customer's existing arrangement
inputs: current approved contract clauses and price options
verified customer identity and existing arrangement

steps.what: Negotiate contracts for prearranged funeral services with the customer and clarify preferences, obligations and unresolved terms
inputs: checked negotiation reference pack
actual customer preferences and questions
outputs: discussed service choices and negotiated terms

steps.what: Enter negotiated choices and prepare the complete proposed contract and customer delivery details
inputs: discussed service choices and negotiated terms
current approved contract clauses and price options
verified customer identity and delivery address
outputs: complete proposed contract with delivery recipient

steps.what: Verify all negotiated terms and approve the final contract and named recipient for issue
inputs: complete proposed contract with delivery recipient

steps.what: Send the approved final prearranged funeral contract to the approved customer recipient
inputs: approved contract issue packet v1

steps.what: Save the exact approved issued contract in its existing contract record
inputs: approved contract issue packet v1
issued contract and delivery receipt

tasks.design: Use the {CLM} reference view and native clause templates to assemble a contract from choices the manager actually records. The manager conducts negotiations, checks the final terms and recipient, and separately authorises issue and storage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contract options and case details may require repeated navigation; a conversation does not supply structured choices automatically.
tasks.enabler_now: Native clause selection and field validation can reduce assembly without negotiating or interpreting preferences.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive preferences, affordability and unusual commitments require human discussion and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertainty or pressure and ensuring the customer understands what is proposed.

ambition.what: No additional service or decision right is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for contract and customer access; review permitted personal-data fields

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: contract systems can assemble approved clauses from selected options and retain issued versions.

assumptions: Boundary covers manager negotiation, contract preparation and issue; customer signature and subsequent service performance are separate work and yield no claimed saving here.

The manager manually captures customer identity confirmation, selected services, prices, exceptions and recipient in s3. Its retained twelve hours include capture, nonstandard drafting and checking; no transcript or structured conversation output is assumed.

Authorised contract owners maintain approved clauses and option prices in ordinary existing work; this proposal's template upkeep is separately charged. Native configuration is tested first; freeform exceptional terms remain manual.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system send and save remain fully retained; no saving is assigned to runtime or customer effort.
Any change to contract or recipient after s4 invalidates both approvals.
unknowns: Proportion of contracts needing nonstandard terms
research_questions: Can native templates reproduce one actual contract without losing an exception?
How much assembly remains after recording negotiated choices?

already_counted.description: Capture terms and check template assembly including exceptions

incremental.description: Check option-to-clause mappings when standard terms change

approvals.approved_version: approved contract issue packet v1 including recipient; edits void approval
approved contract issue packet v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 14 minus 1 upkeep gives 13. High allows three more hours of unusual-clause work; low covers already configured templates or predominantly bespoke contracts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain funeral home goals, policies and procedures to staff

steps.what: Find the current goals, policies or procedures relevant to the staff explanation
inputs: versioned approved goals, policies and procedures
actual staff question or change to explain

steps.what: Prepare the staff explanation using selected approved passages and manager-written practical examples
inputs: checked current policy passages
actual staff question or change to explain

steps.what: Explain goals, policies or procedures to staff members and discuss practical questions
inputs: prepared staff explanation
actual staff questions
outputs: actual explanation delivered and unresolved staff questions

tasks.design: Configure version filters and reusable approved passage blocks in the {DOCS}. The manager supplies examples and explains the procedure in person, resolving actual questions in the discussion; no follow-up note or approval workflow is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current policy and assembling approved passages can interrupt explanation preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and reusable text blocks can reduce navigation and copying without generating policy interpretations.
tasks.still_hard: Applying procedures sensitively to particular staff concerns remains human work.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, invite challenge and explain how a policy applies to a difficult funeral situation.

ambition.what: No additional decision authority or service is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for policy access and checking current reference ownership

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: versioned document libraries support metadata filters and reusable approved passages.

assumptions: Boundary includes finding current policy passages, preparing a relevant explanation and explaining it live. The task does not establish a separate follow-up record, so none is assumed or added.
Policy owners supply document id, version, approval status and applicable topic. Without reliable metadata the manager verifies versions manually in s1; no free classification is assumed.
s2 retains manager-written examples and relevance checks. Actual staff questions are resolved in s3; no transcript or structured discussion output is assumed.
Native configuration first. Shares and reductions are unmeasured scenarios, not an asserted existing administrative baseline. If no separate preparation is actually done, its proposed gain is zero.
No persistent write, send or self-approval of a routine note is introduced. If a real organisation requires a record, measure and split that actual work before redesigning it.
unknowns: Whether current policy metadata is reliable
Whether separate preparation actually occurs for these explanations
research_questions: Does a current-version filter reduce preparation on actual staff questions?
Can passage blocks be reused without removing important context?

already_counted.description: Check selected passages and write relevant examples

incremental.description: Maintain explanation passage links when policies change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 11.2 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 10.7. High allows 2.7 additional hours checking contextual exceptions; low applies where current filters and blocks already exist.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule funeral home and contract employee work hours

steps.what: Check funeral bookings, employee availability, skills and contract-hour constraints for the roster period
inputs: arranger-maintained actual funeral bookings with times, locations and staffing requirements
staff-maintained availability and HCM-maintained skills and contractual hours
outputs: checked staffing requirements and availability snapshot

steps.what: Construct a draft schedule matching available qualified employees to required service hours
inputs: checked staffing requirements and availability snapshot
manager-validated hard scheduling constraints
outputs: draft schedule and explicit uncovered or conflicting shifts

steps.what: Resolve coverage conflicts, suitability and fairness issues and complete the employee work schedule and delivery list
inputs: draft schedule and explicit uncovered or conflicting shifts
actual staff constraints and manager knowledge
outputs: complete final employee schedule and exact delivery recipients

steps.what: Approve the final roster, effective period and exact recipients after all changes
inputs: complete final employee schedule and exact delivery recipients

steps.what: Commit the approved employee work schedule in its existing scheduling system
inputs: approved roster issue packet v1

steps.what: Send the approved work hours to the named internal and contract employees
inputs: approved roster issue packet v1
committed work schedule

tasks.design: Test the native scheduling module of the {OPS_SYSTEM} using checked booking requirements and authorised {HCM} fields. A constraint-based draft exposes uncovered work; the manager resolves suitability and fairness, approves the finished roster, then commits and issues that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service bookings, skills and availability may need checking in different views, and feasible schedules still need manual assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured scheduling constraints can produce a feasible draft without scoring employee behaviour or inferring sensitive traits.
tasks.still_hard: Last-minute funerals, staff preferences, appropriate interpersonal skills and exceptional availability need manager judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Allocate difficult duties fairly and recognise when a mathematically feasible pairing is unsuitable.

ambition.what: Compare alternative coverage for an additional funeral before accepting its time slot.

reach.task: Review scheduling constraints for workload fairness
reach.learn: Interpret contractual hours, agreed availability and national rules with staff representatives.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-15 for booking and HCM access and applicable employee consultation under national rules

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scheduling systems can apply explicit availability, skill and hour constraints and flag infeasible shifts.

assumptions: Boundary is manager scheduling, checking and issuing hours; staff supplying availability and performing funeral services remain outside the focal denominator and receive no claimed saving.

Booking staff already record event id, start/end, location and required roles; HCM owners supply employee id, skills, contract hours and dated availability. s1 retains correction and manual capture if fields are missing; no free new structured capture is assumed.
Native configuration first. Manager validates hard constraints before s2; no model makes employment judgements. s2 retains solver review and reruns, while s3 retains all suitability decisions.

All shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. System runtime earns no saving. Same-system roster commit stays fully retained; issuing even short messages is separately counted and retained.
Approval binds the roster and its exact recipients. Changes after s4 require renewed approval; contract-employee delivery makes s6 an external action.
unknowns: Existing native roster solver and booking export capabilities
Completeness of staff availability and skill data
research_questions: Can a configured solver reproduce an accepted recent roster and expose its exceptions?
How many manual corrections are needed after availability import?

already_counted.description: Inspect proposed assignments and uncovered hours and rerun after corrections

incremental.description: Maintain skill and scheduling-rule mappings and regression-check changed constraints

approvals.approved_version: approved roster issue packet v1; any schedule edit voids approval
approved roster issue packet v1 including exact recipients; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 30 minus 2 upkeep gives 28. High allows six extra hours for last-minute booking and availability exceptions; low applies if an existing scheduler already supplies the same draft or manual corrections remove the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager spends less time finding current options and assembling rosters or contract fields; responsibility for sensitive service choices, contracts and staff allocations stays with the manager.
reach: Assess proposed service contribution with a financial manager after learning cost allocation.
Review scheduling fairness with human resources after learning applicable contractual constraints.
skills_to_grow: Test scheduling constraints and review exceptions
role.ambitious_version: Test whether a proposed community service can be delivered at an appropriate price with a feasible staff plan before offering it.
